we study theoretically the spatiotemporal response of a lipid membrane submitted to a local chemical change of its environment , taking into account the time - dependent profile of the reagent concentration due to diffusion in the solution above the membrane . 
 we show that the effect of the evolution of the reagent concentration profile becomes negligible after some time . 
 it then becomes possible to extract interesting properties of the membrane response to the chemical modification .

 this behavior is driven by intermonolayer friction .

 the dependence of the suppression on the magnetic field strength is greater at longer periods and higher formation heights .
